newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German first-quarter GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German first-quarter GDP.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on news that pan-German gross domestic product (GDP) rose by seasonally- and calendar-adjusted half a percentage point in the first quarter of 1997 from the final quarter of 1996. Year-on-year, GDP rose 1.4 percent in the first quarter.

LOTHAR HESSLER, BOND ANALYST AT TRINKAUS & BURKHARDT: "The quarter-on-quarter growth rate is slightly higher than we had expected; it shows that the economy is growing moderately. But I think that full-year 1997 growth will be slightly less than the government's growth forecast of 2.5 percent and that could add to the government's budget problems. The growth is driven by exports and capital equipment spending.

"The figures are in line with our expectations. The important number is the 0.5 percent increase in the first quarter. We have an unusual calendar in the first quarter. Annualised this means 2.0 percent growth, and I think this is actually the true growth rate for the first quarter."
SONJA GIBBS AT NOMURA IN LONDON

"Although a lot of it was driven by exports, we must also have seen a little bit on the investment side in terms of stock building. What this does suggest is that growth for the rest of the year may surprise on the upside. Depending on the composition of GDP, we could see a little bit stronger growth than the markets have been anticipating, which could be good for the tax revenue position in Germany. Factoring these figures in for the whole year we might even get to the government's growth target of 2.5 percent."
